full_judgment:
2. Mr. Moinul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner has submitted that the only point for consideration before the Court  is whether to grant leave or not and that the question of limitation is to be decided by the Division Bench considering the appeal, if leave is granted. 

 3. Mr. T.H. Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party has submitted that application for leave must be filed before the expiry of the period of limitation otherwise the rule prescribing the time limit would be rendered nugatory. 

 6. The present application has been filed 99 days after the delivery of judgment. No explanation has been given for this long delay in filing the application for leave, when normally it should have been done immediately after the delivery of the judgment. Mr. Moinul Huq has argued that the question of limitation, if any, could only be decided by the Division Bench considering the appeal. There is no dispute in that. But the question is, what is the duty of the Court when a leave application is presented for its consideration in a time barred appeal. Supposing a Court  decides to overlook the time limit and grants leave in a time barred appeal, yet the Division Bench considering the appeal may in its discretion reject the cause shown as insufficient and dismiss the appeal as time barred. Can any Court  be expected to consciously ignore such an eventuality and still entertain a prayer for leave in a time barred appeal?. Granting leave in such a case, I am afraid, would only be an exercise in futility. 

 7. The learned Advocates could not cite any decision in support of their respective contentions either of this Court or of the then East Pakistan High Court or of the Supreme Court of Pakistan. I have however been able to lay my hands on one decision of the then East. Pakistan High Court in the case of Md. Sharif Khan Vs. Akhtar Hossain Khan, 5 D.L.R. at page 549. In the said case the learned Judge while rejecting three applications for leave under clause 15 of the Letters Patent observed that the prayer for leave should be made orally and immediately after the delivery of the judgment and further that it should be made by the same Advocate who had argued the appeal originally and not by another Advocate. The learned Judge rejected two of the applications on the first ground as well as on merits while he rejected the third application as time barred since it was presented after 60 days. With due respect to the learned Judge, I have been unable to persuade myself to agree with his lordship's observations above. When the time limit for filing the appeal in 60 days, I do not find any reason to restrict the petitioner's right to pray for leave any time within the period of limitation or to fetter the petitioner's right to have a lawyer of his own choice. But, I fully agree that the application for leave should not be entertained when the appeal is time barred. I therefore find no substance in the contentions of Mr. Moinul Huq.
